questions.question_text: Triangle $A$ has a base of $16\text{ cm}$ and a perpendicular height of $6\text{ cm}$. Triangle $B$ has a base of $12\text{ cm}$ and a perpendicular height of $8\text{ cm}$. Which has the larger area?

options.why: Paired $B$’s base with $A$’s height, calculating $\tfrac{1}{2}\times12\times6$.
Paired $A$’s base with $B$’s height, calculating $\tfrac{1}{2}\times16\times8$.
Added the base and the height for each triangle and halved the sums.

questions.solution_text:
$A_{A}=\frac{16\times6}{2}$
$=48\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_{B}=\frac{12\times8}{2}$
$=48\text{ cm}^{2}$
Neither is larger: both triangles have an area of $48\text{ cm}^{2}$.

Both smaller triangles have the same perpendicular height, $9\text{ m}$.
$A_{\text{left}}=\frac{14\times9}{2}$
$=63\text{ m}^{2}$
$A_{\text{right}}=\frac{6\times9}{2}$
$=27\text{ m}^{2}$

The difference is $36\text{ m}^{2}$.
